title: HelixBench implementation specification · UX v4
authority: User selected latest UX v4 while preserving existing scientific capabilities.

screens.name: Home
screens.layout: Labeled workspace navigation; Import sequence and Try a sample on first use; exact recent records and resumable work on populated Home; contextual next steps at right.
requirements: First launch offers an empty personal workspace and an explicit sample choice. Existing installations restore their own workspace without replacing it with demo data.
Recent rows resolve a typed identity or a normalized file path, never a row index or display-name match. Missing files offer Locate or Remove without altering the document.
Resume a task, notebook entry or saved analysis with its selection, query, return route and persistence status. Display unsaved documents separately from saved files.
Project/folder changes validate parent existence and cycles. Bulk tag/export/close operates on the reviewed ID set; canceling a dirty-document close leaves the remaining queue intact.
Calendar and work totals are derived from local records; date navigation changes scope without modifying records. An empty calendar day is not a loading failure.
edgeCases: Fresh config versus existing config with no open document.
Recent path moved, inaccessible, duplicated with different spelling, or points to a newer native-file format.
Two documents share a name; the intended stable ID must open.
One dirty document in a multi-close operation fails to save or the user cancels.
A task or entry disappears between list rendering and activation.
Sample workspace exit, personal copy and restarting the application do not merge sample and personal records.
flow: Return to Home with updated status

screens.name: Map
screens.layout: Document identity and saved/draft state; six scientific views; editable map with zoom and readable-annotation alternative; selection-bound right tools panel.
requirements: Map representation (Plasmid/Linear) is independent of biological topology. A display switch does not edit the molecule.
All coordinates displayed to users are 1-based inclusive; internal Range remains zero-based start plus length. Circular origin-spanning selections retain ordered segments.
Feature, primer and enzyme selection synchronizes the map, list and inspector. Clear selection removes dependent actions rather than retaining the previous record.
Display toggles, zoom, fit, center and minimap remain available. Readable annotation lists carry the same IDs and coordinates when labels are dense.
Mutating topology, origin or sequence direction has an impact preview for affected annotations/primers and remains undoable; analyses retain their captured input.
edgeCases: Empty sequence, one-base sequence, very long sequence or dense overlapping annotations.
Drag across the circular origin; reverse-strand feature; discontiguous feature segments.
Map display is Linear while topology is Circular, and the reverse.
Selection or document changes after opening a tool.
Zoom/minimap movement must not accidentally edit a feature.
Undo after a topology/origin edit restores selection and annotations; read-only display changes do not mark dirty.
flow: Apply and return to the same map region

screens.name: Sequence
screens.layout: Named sequence and version; virtualized double-stranded base rows; explicit range/strand/frame; Find bar; same contextual tools as Map.
requirements: Paste and replacement preview the original, recognized alphabet and every meaningful transformation before mutation. Whitespace normalization is reported; unsupported symbols are not silently discarded.
Editing updates affected feature/primer coordinates using the existing domain operations and preserves an undo checkpoint. Cancellation changes neither data nor dirty state.
DNA/protein/name search modes stay distinct. Hit navigation, highlighting and search recents retain the query and coordinate system.
Complement, six-frame translation, ORFs, genetic code and custom/history color modes preserve existing scientific behavior. Protein output is not stored as DNA.
Source-view switching retains the active document, draft, range, strand, search position and scroll anchor. Clipboard failure leaves selection and content unchanged.
edgeCases: Paste contains U, gaps, digits, Unicode, lowercase, IUPAC symbols or invalid bytes.
Replacing a region changes length or overlaps an annotation boundary.
Search has no hits, wraps to the first hit, matches the reverse strand or uses an invalid alphabet.
Cut succeeds in mutation only when required clipboard handling succeeds.
Changing the genetic code changes computed translations without corrupting annotations.
Window resizing and large text do not move the caret to an unrelated coordinate.
flow: Save or undo without losing the position

screens.name: Features
screens.layout: Searchable/sortable feature table with selected-record inspector, explicit Add/Edit/Delete, detection preview and reusable feature library.
requirements: Fields include name, kind, segments, direction, color, note, product, translation flag, genetic code, first-codon-Met option and frame offset. Preserve existing IDs when editing.
Segment parsing validates linear bounds, circular spans, empty ranges and supported multi-segment syntax; show errors beside the segment input.
Detect Common Features and bulk auto-annotation display candidate positions, strand, source motif and conflicts before applying a selected set.
Deleting a feature is an undoable document edit. Routine completion uses an inline status or toast; it does not require a second confirmation screen.
Column visibility, filters and sort do not change selection identity. A readable list is synchronized with map and sequence views.
edgeCases: Duplicate names, empty name, invalid coordinates, wrapped segments and reverse-direction CDS.
Frame offset outside 0–2; partial codon; absent product; a translation flag on a noncoding feature.
Overlapping/duplicate detection candidates and ambiguous motif matches.
Library motif is empty or incompatible with the sequence alphabet.
Bulk annotation across dirty, empty and closed documents preserves per-document outcomes.
Delete the selected row after sorting; clear the inspector and keep Undo available.
flow: Inspect its range and biological meaning
Save and highlight it on Map / Sequence

screens.name: Primers
screens.layout: Primer/pair table with binding context, length/GC/Tm/structure indicators; selected pair inspector; separate design and PCR setup/results.
requirements: Primer sequence is entered 5′→3′ and validated using supported primer symbols; preserve phosphorylation, description and color. Display the assumed hybridization/Tm method and conditions.
Design setup distinguishes the current selection anchor from the proposed amplification target. Show start, target length, target Tm, 5′ overhang and explicit forward/reverse candidate selection.
Candidates include length, GC, Tm and hairpin/self-dimer indicators. An unselected or stale candidate cannot be added as an unrelated pair.
PCR captures template version, both primer IDs/sequences, binding positions/directions and feature-copy policy. Open the product as a new, independently identified document.
No binding or incompatible orientation is a successful diagnostic outcome, distinct from a computation error. Existing pair/primer capability remains available from the owning page within two clicks.
edgeCases: Blank/invalid sequence, ambiguous binding, multiple sites and reverse-primer orientation.
Selection changes after setup; a linked primer is edited or deleted before Run.
Overhang is valid but changes the product length; primer body and overhang must be distinguished.
Target start/length exceeds a linear molecule or spans a circular origin.
No valid candidates, hairpin warning and no predicted PCR product.
Product creation with feature copy, repeated product names and canceled save retains source identity.
flow: Continue directly to PCR or assembly

screens.name: Enzymes
screens.layout: Enzyme set and composable cut/region filters; cut-site table; restriction analysis setup and fragment/gel results with input provenance.
requirements: Preserve enzyme sets, unique/double/non-cutter filters, cut counts, methylation-sensitive filtering and anywhere/selection/custom-region search.
A whole-sequence digest is not silently restricted to the selected promoter. Show topology, scope, enzyme set and input revision before running.
Results list fragments, lengths, cut positions and method assumptions; a gel is an additional view with a labeled ladder and migration model.
Zero cut sites is a completed result. Linear and circular fragment accounting use the domain engine rather than fixed prototype values.
Filter reset restores scope predictably; filtering never changes biological topology or the saved chosen-enzyme set without an explicit edit.
edgeCases: No enzyme selected, no sites, one cut in circular DNA, coincident cuts and ambiguous bases.
Custom interval is invalid, empty or wraps the origin.
A non-cutter filter combined with a region filter produces no rows.
Fragment lengths and topology-specific totals remain correct at boundary cuts.
Unknown enzyme name in an older document is reported and retained for review.
Editing the source while a digest runs creates an older-input result rather than writing into the new source context.
flow: Open digest and gel with the chosen set

screens.name: History
screens.layout: Separate edit Undo/Redo history and persistent named checkpoints; current version marker; compare/restore preview; linked result provenance.
requirements: Undo/Redo act on the current document edit stack. Named versions are persistent checkpoints and are not substitutes for Undo.
Restore previews changes to sequence, features and primers and creates an intentional current state; older result provenance remains tied to the original snapshot.
Use durable revision IDs instead of list indexes in persisted references. The existing 20-checkpoint retention cap cannot erase an input referenced by a retained result.
Dirty-state calculation remains correct after save, undo-to-saved, redo and branching edits. Mark unsaved versions explicitly.
Canceling restore leaves current state, version list and selection untouched. A failed native save does not falsely mark the document clean.
edgeCases: Undo at the first edit, redo at the last edit, branch after undo and undo back to the saved point.
Empty version list, repeated labels and restoration of an unavailable snapshot.
Pinned result input reaches the checkpoint-retention boundary.
Restore while another document is active or an analysis result is pending.
Clock changes affect timestamp ordering but not stable revision identity.
Legacy version indexes are migrated once and are never used as permanent cross-record IDs.
flow: Choose an operation or saved version
Return to the recovered document with an undo route

screens.name: Notebook
screens.layout: Entry list and document editor with blank/template choice; linked inputs; structured tables; separate text-save, table-submit and review status.
requirements: New entries are genuinely blank. A template adds declared headings/table schemas, never unrelated measurements or a silent source link.
Structured result submission validates columns, required values and source links; creates reusable results and records exactly which rows were submitted.
Capture immutable submitted revisions for review. Draft edits and submitted snapshots remain distinguishable; approved/archived content is protected.
Review is a local workflow in this release. Actor labels and local status recording must not imply a network message, authenticated remote reviewer or public sharing.
Draft → InReview → ChangesRequested → InReview → Approved/Archived transitions retain entry ID, result IDs, source revisions, comments and revision number.
Plate snapshots attached to an entry stay immutable after live inventory changes.
edgeCases: Blank title, missing project, deleted source and invalid/ragged result rows.
Cancel template application or switch templates after writing notes.
Submit twice, amend a submitted table or persist only some of a multi-store result submission.
Request review before required results exist, reject with a comment and resubmit the same entry.
Attempt to edit an approved, archived or submitted read-only snapshot.
An automation table with 96 submitted rows and a manual table with two draft rows remain separate data groups.
flow: Submit or write back a table
Review / request changes / approve with clear status

screens.name: Registry
screens.layout: Entity table with kind/schema and stable identity; scientific relationships; related samples; active/archived views; dependency-aware deletion.
requirements: Preserve plasmid, strain and primer schemas; federate biologic/oligo records by typed store references instead of inventing a shared numeric ID namespace.
Open, edit, archive and restore the exact selected entity after sorting or filtering. Display names are not foreign keys.
Archive hides active rows but retains identity and references. Permanent delete requires exact ID confirmation and an explicit dependency summary.

Block deletion when an active dependency needs a live record or a historical result lacks a durable source snapshot. Historical results with complete immutable provenance may retain a tombstone after deletion.
Successful deletion clears selection, inspector actions, active-record cues and search results. Historical output cannot resurrect a deleted source through View source.
CSV import reviews column mapping, row errors, duplicates and partial outcome before persisting. Relationships reject self-links and nonexistent target IDs.
edgeCases: Same name across kinds/stores; missing linked file; renamed document; archived reference.
Delete is canceled, ID confirmation differs, a new dependency appears or disk persistence fails.
Delete a source whose result has a snapshot versus a result whose provenance is incomplete.
Mixed valid/invalid CSV rows, duplicate headers, quoted commas and repeated import.
Deleting a row after sort/filter leaves the correct remaining selection or no selection.
Archive PR-001 must never show DNA-001 in confirmation, completion or restore.
flow: Save and verify the entity in context

screens.name: Inventory
screens.layout: Storage hierarchy and plate grid; separate inspect-well and bulk-selection context; assignment review; transfer mapping; immutable snapshot access.
requirements: Scientific entity identity is distinct from physical container/sample identity. Store typed entity references, container IDs and explicit quantity/concentration units.
A well control carries its own plate ID and coordinate; bulk assignment carries the complete reviewed set of well IDs. Row indexes and a fixed A1–A4 string are not action payloads.
Assignment reviews previous contents, proposed entity, role and quantity; occupied wells require explicit replacement review.

Transfer validates all source volumes, destination occupancy, units and mappings before committing the entire reviewed operation. Source subtraction, destination addition and audit use a recoverable persistence boundary.
Refreshing or returning from an operation updates occupancy, counts, selected-well details and filters. Earlier notebook snapshots do not change.
Validate storage parent/cycle rules and plate dimensions; barcode keyboard input/paste is lookup data, not evidence of camera/scanner integration.
edgeCases: Empty and occupied wells, A1/H12 boundaries, another plate with the same coordinate, empty selection and bulk selection.
Negative, zero, nonfinite quantity; missing legacy concentration unit; incompatible mass/volume units.
Destination is occupied, source equals destination, duplicate destinations or source volume is insufficient.
One of four reviewed transfers fails before commit or persistence fails after staging.
A storage node is moved into its own descendant or a selected container is deleted.
Live updates leave immutable experiment snapshots unchanged; inspect-well does not silently alter the bulk selected set.
flow: Save or snapshot into a notebook entry

screens.name: Workflows
screens.layout: Named tasks/requests and flowchart; selected task details, required inputs, output mapping, blocker and next executable step.
requirements: Every row opens its own task or request ID and current status. Assignee, due date and source references remain visible.
A task with missing required mappings is blocked with a field-level remedy; repairing it does not silently execute the next step.
Request draft/sent and task execution status are distinct local state machines. Send records a local transition, not a remote delivery.
Execute a reviewed graph step against captured inputs; advance only after its outputs persist successfully. Reject missing steps, cycles or incompatible output types.
Resume retains the run cursor, selected task and mapping; cancellation or failed writeback does not skip or duplicate a step.
edgeCases: Missing/deleted input, invalid mapping key, duplicate task title, no selected task and inconsistent assignee label.
A downstream mapping fails after an upstream step succeeds.
Repeated Execute, status edit during execution and a completed step invoked again.
Malformed flowchart, dangling edge, branch with no output or a cycle.
Request validation fails or local persistence fails after Send is selected.
Returning from Notebook or Registry restores the same task rather than opening a generic worklist.
flow: Enter output and complete or fail
See next step and audit event

screens.name: Insights
screens.layout: Local dashboard blocks with visible source scope, grouping/filter parameters, chart/table alternatives, refresh status and CSV export.
requirements: Identify the underlying dataset and its local scope before interpreting a block. Display the query/grouping/filter assumptions and refresh timestamp.
Distinguish no source records, no matching filtered rows, a missing parameter, query failure and unavailable source references.
Chart axes, units and category legends are labeled. Offer a readable data table and stable-ID links back to the contributing records.
Parameters and dataset revision form the cache key; changing a filter or source invalidates stale aggregates without replacing a different block.
CSV export uses the displayed scope, correct quoting and an explicit local destination; cancellation or failed write does not report export success.
edgeCases: Empty dataset, a category with no values, missing numeric values and nonfinite input.
Filter excludes all rows; selected grouping column no longer exists.
Source records change while aggregation runs.
Long labels, many categories and horizontal scrolling at smaller widths.
Dataset is local but a referenced source file is inaccessible or deleted.
CSV contains commas, quotes, newlines, Unicode and values that spreadsheet applications interpret as formulas.
flow: Export the named source or displayed result

screens.name: Automation
screens.layout: Draft/published pipeline configuration; input review and mapping; run history by ID; running/cancel/recovery states; output and writeback audit.
requirements: Published configurations have an immutable revision reference. Editing a draft does not mutate an in-flight run or an earlier completed run.
CSV ingestion handles quoting, newlines, encoding and row shape. Validate required identifiers and mapping before any writeback.
Running, cancel-requested, canceled, completed, failed and partial-write outcomes are distinct. Do not present a Cancel action when the actual stage cannot safely support it.
Persist run IDs, source fingerprint, parameters, staged outputs and per-row writeback identities. A retry cannot repeat successful output writes.
Recovery of a validation-only failure starts a reviewed new run. Recovery of a partial write first reconciles retained output IDs and the remaining row set.
An output table and linked notebook keep submitted automation rows separate from existing manual draft rows.
edgeCases: Empty/malformed CSV, duplicate headers, missing row IDs, quoted commas/newlines, UTF-8 BOM and repeated source input.
Template deleted/unpublished after review; unknown pipeline step; changed destination schema.
Cancel during parsing, before commit or after some writes; application closes during a run.
Persistence succeeds for outputs but not run history/audit; restart must reconcile the journal.
Double-click Start, retry an already completed run or resume an uncertain partial outcome.
R-017 and R-018 remain distinct run details; no history row opens another run just because it shares a pipeline.

screens.name: Split
screens.layout: Two named inputs with active-pane indication; independent/synchronized navigation; pair/multiple alignment setup and saved alignments.
requirements: Each pane identifies document ID, revision, topology and active selection. Tool actions specify the pane or the captured input set.
Choosing another input honors its dirty-document guard and keeps the other pane intact. The same document in both panes is an explicit choice.
Alignment captures pair order, reindex option, scoring/method and source versions; saved alignments have their own stable ID.
Preserve existing pair and progressive multiple alignment, consensus and identity outputs; do not turn a display comparison into sequence mutation.
Opening a saved result whose source is closed or deleted shows retained provenance and offers a safe source-resolution path.
edgeCases: No second document, same input twice, one empty input, linear versus circular and reversed input order.
Selection is made in the right pane but a tool tries to use the left pane.
Circular auto-reindex changes coordinate presentation; preserve an explicit mapping.
Source edited during a long alignment or removed while loading a saved alignment.
Very long sequences or many documents require budget review, background work and cancellation.
Delete a saved alignment after sorting; retain the underlying documents.

screens.name: Biologics
screens.layout: Biologic identity/format with chain selection, components and numbering; explicit protein-input analysis; related record/sample links.
requirements: Fields preserve name, format, numbering and all chains. Chain identity, sequence type and length remain explicit across tools.
Protein analysis consumes the selected protein or an explicitly reviewed translation product. A DNA document cannot silently become HC-014.
Display molecular properties and alignment with method/units/assumptions; save a result linked to the actual protein chain revision.
A numbering/annotation scheme is labeled by the implementation actually present; unsupported regions or formats remain visible as limitations.
Deleting or editing a chain reviews dependent biologic/result links and preserves immutable historical input.
edgeCases: Missing chain, unsupported amino acid, stop/gap symbols, unusual chain length and duplicate names.
Selected light chain differs from the default heavy chain; never substitute another chain.
Biologic format expects a chain that is missing or cannot be classified.
Protein comparison is blank, invalid or the wrong molecular type.
Numbering scheme cannot assign a residue; do not invent coverage.

screens.name: Chemistry
screens.layout: Compound list and supported-SMILES inspection; substructure search; reaction identities/equivalents; salt/solvate forms and physical material lots.
requirements: Validate the supported SMILES subset before deriving formula/mass. Unsupported stereochemistry or syntax is not silently interpreted as a fully supported structure.
Separate compound identity, reaction identity and material-lot quantity/location. Use stable IDs for reaction participants and form references.
Reaction input identifies reactant/product and positive finite equivalents; calculated changes show the assumptions of the local model.
Substructure search uses the implemented matching semantics and shows no-match independently from parse failure.
Compound/reaction deletion checks references. Repeated display names and a changed selected row cannot redirect a save/delete to another compound.
edgeCases: Unbalanced ring/branch/bracket syntax, unsupported element/bond/stereochemistry and malformed charge.
Zero/negative/nonfinite equivalents or missing participant.
Compound is referenced by a reaction, lot, registry relation or result.
A salt/solvate form changes molecular mass while a lot retains its own quantity unit.
Substructure query fails to parse or matches no compounds.
Formula/mass computation is unavailable for an unsupported structure; never display a fabricated number.

screens.layout: Named RNA/modified-oligo list; direction, sequence, chemistry pattern and monomer inspection; HELM import/export and related identity.
requirements: Validate RNA/oligo input using its own alphabet and modification model; never pass it through DNA cleaning without explicit conversion review.
Preserve name, sequence, selected pattern, modification code and HELM source. Show the modified positions before applying a pattern.
Sequence order, direction and terminal chemistry remain explicit. Properties reflect the selected oligo, not a generic example.
HELM parsing reports unsupported monomers/connections and preserves original text for correction; export describes supported coverage.
Delete/edit reviews dependent references and retains historical result provenance.
edgeCases: Mixed T/U, DNA pasted as RNA, unsupported monomer, terminal modification and empty sequence.
HELM record has malformed syntax or a monomer outside the local library.
A modification pattern targets a missing position or conflicts with existing chemistry.
Same name with different chemistry or an edited oligo still selected by row index.
No property model exists for a chosen modification; show unavailable rather than a guessed value.
Round-trip supported HELM without changing residue order or chemistry.
flow: Apply or revise modifications and keep a clear change summary

screens.name: In Vivo
screens.layout: Study identity/species/strain; animals and cohorts; measurement timeline; explicit-unit calculation helper; study schedule and exports.
requirements: Keep study and animal IDs distinct. Measurements bind to the selected animal and date/day, not the currently highlighted row after a filter.
Weight and measurement units are visible. Numeric inputs must be finite and compatible with the domain model; conversions are explicit.
Cohort randomization captures seed, group count and the animal set; preview imbalance and avoid silently re-randomizing an established assignment.
The calculation helper displays formula, input units and output units and remains a calculation aid; no treatment recommendation is inferred from a prototype fixture.
Study deletion reviews animals, measurements and downstream references; canceled or failed persistence retains the existing study.
edgeCases: No study/animal selected, duplicate animal tag within a study, missing species and deleted study.
Negative/nonfinite weight or measurement; missing unit; duplicate day entries.
Group count exceeds animal count, empty cohort, unequal groups and repeated randomization with the same seed.
Concentration is zero or units are incompatible in the calculation helper.
A measurement edit occurs after a cohort summary was computed.
Export includes animal/study IDs and units without conflating identical tags in different studies.

screens.name: Bioprocess
screens.layout: Recipe/unit-operation definition; draft/executing/completed/aborted runs; operator steps; replicate conditions/titer and cross-run comparison.
requirements: Recipe identity and an execution run are different objects. Capture the recipe revision and input lots when a run starts.
Start, complete, abort and step-completion actions obey the domain state machine; a completed/aborted run cannot silently restart.
Durations, conditions, titer and quantities have visible units and finite values. Preserve the selected run/replicate during editing.
Comparison identifies every run, recipe, replicate and condition rather than displaying unlabeled aggregate values.
Deleting a run or recipe reviews dependent records; physical lot consumption and result recording use recoverable operation boundaries when implemented.
edgeCases: No recipe selected, no unit operations, empty name/product and a recipe changed after run planning.
Start twice, complete with incomplete required steps, abort at a boundary or toggle a step in a locked run.
Negative/nonfinite duration or titer and mixed condition units.
Duplicate replicate labels and comparison of incompatible process/measurement units.
Run deletion while a computation or comparison is open.
Restart after a partially persisted operation retains run identity and does not silently consume lots twice.
flow: Complete or abort with a clear audit trail

decisions: UX v4 defines target interaction and visual behavior. Existing scientific capabilities are preserved; code/schema evidence controls what currently exists. Prototype fixtures never define actual numerical results.
Keep the Rust 2021 workspace, native GPUI shell and domain/appcore/storage boundaries. Do not replace the UI with a web shell or egui.

Remain local-first, offline and account-free. Review/request/audience states are local workflow records. Real remote delivery, authentication and multi-user authorization require a separate approved scope.

Keep DnaSequence as DNA. Route RNA/oligo and protein inputs through explicit typed representations/module handoffs. Until a molecule can be represented safely, block its commit with original input retained; never clean protein into DNA.

Add UUID-backed document/revision/result/operation identities while preserving existing store-local u64 keys. Persist identities once; importing as a copy remints document identity and retains original provenance.

Block active live dependencies and historical outputs lacking an immutable input snapshot. A historical result with complete provenance may retain a tombstone after source deletion. Archive is the safe default.
Retain the current checkpoint behavior for unreferenced history, but pin or separately snapshot every source used by a retained result. The current 20-checkpoint cap cannot break provenance.
Compute from an immutable captured input; validate before writeback; persist a recoverable operation journal for cross-store mutations. Offer cancellation only at a supported stage.
Feature entry is within two navigation clicks from its owning page. Labeled page navigation is one click. Data entry, OS file picking and necessary safety confirmation are measured separately.

Use one persistent shell, contextual right panel, modal decisions for consequential operations and inline/toast completion for routine actions. Figma feedback-content frames are not instructions to build hundreds of blocking modals.

Introduce native schema v2 for durable identities/provenance. Read v1, migrate in memory and save only on explicit user action, with a recoverable backup. Newer unsupported versions remain read-protected and explain the required app update.

Use engine-specific method names and disclose implemented limitations. CRISPR scores are local Rule-Set-2-style/CFD implementations, local BLAST is a seed-and-extend search, and chemistry supports a SMILES subset. Independent method validation precedes stronger scientific claims.

journeys.name: First meaningful sequence result
steps: Home → Import source
Recognized-content and transformation review
Open the exact sequence ID/revision
Choose restriction analysis with explicit scope
Review settings → run against captured input
Inspect completed/no-match/failed outcome
Save named output with provenance
Leave → find by recent work/search → reopen the same result

journeys.name: Blank sequence
steps: Create → enter supported DNA and topology
Review valid input or correct field errors
Create a newly identified document
Edit/save/analyze its own sequence
Refind the new document; do not return to the demo

journeys.name: Sample to personal work
steps: Choose labeled sample
Inspect/run within sample namespace
Exit safely or review personal copy
Allocate independent document ID/revision
Run a new personal analysis with a new result ID

journeys.name: Notebook and results
steps: Create a blank entry or deliberately apply a template
Link a reviewed source revision
Write notes and add a structured table
Validate/submit result rows
Capture a submitted local-review revision
Record changes requested → amend draft → resubmit
Inspect the correct read-only submitted revision

journeys.name: Physical sample custody
steps: Choose storage/container and inspect an exact well
Choose a single assignment or an explicit multi-well set
Review existing/proposed contents and units
Validate source/destination transfer mappings
Commit a recoverable operation
Refresh live state and retain immutable notebook snapshots

journeys.name: Archive, delete and retained history
steps: Select exact typed record
Archive/review/restore using the same identity
For permanent delete, confirm ID and revalidate dependencies
Block live/unrecoverable dependencies or commit deletion
Clear selection and caches
Open retained historical result via its snapshot/tombstone

journeys.name: Automation recovery
steps: Review input, immutable pipeline version and output target
Validate parsed rows before writeback
Start a uniquely identified operation
Cancel only at a supported boundary
Inspect completed/failed/partial outcome
Reconcile retained output IDs before recovery
Write remaining outputs without duplication and refind by run ID

journeys.name: Source change and scientific results
steps: Inspect the saved result’s captured input
Edit/save a newer source revision
Label older-input result without overwriting it
Review rerun inputs and allocate a new result ID
Compare method/parameters/outputs and export provenance

tasks.title: Stable identity, revision provenance and migrations

tasks.title: Navigation intents, selection and dirty-work guards

tasks.title: Safe import interpretation and commit

tasks.title: Operation controller, persistence errors and feedback

tasks.title: Command registry and scoped workspace search
tasks.goal: Centralize tool availability/context and implement typed scoped search independent of sequence Find.

tasks.title: First-use Home, samples and resume
tasks.goal: Implement explicit Import/Try sample, isolated sample origin, typed recent-work resume and saved-result refind.

tasks.title: Soft Gallery shell and contextual tools
tasks.goal: Apply central tokens/layout and the selected-context right panel while retaining a readable scientific workspace.

tasks.title: Map, sequence and coordinate synchronization

tasks.title: Feature editing and annotation review
tasks.goal: Preserve feature fields/segments and apply selected annotation proposals through validated document mutations.

tasks.title: Primer design and PCR context
tasks.goal: Bind actual template/pair/candidate identity and parameters to design, diagnostics and independent PCR product creation.

tasks.title: Enzyme filters, digest and history
tasks.goal: Preserve composable enzyme filters, digest accounting, Undo/Redo and named-version compare/restore semantics.

tasks.title: Saved analysis result lifecycle
tasks.goal: Persist actual tool outputs, input snapshots and parameters, then implement save/refind/older-input/rerun/compare/export.

tasks.title: Alignment, split workspace and saved alignments
tasks.goal: Keep pair and multiple alignment behavior with explicit pane/input scope and durable saved-result provenance.

tasks.title: Assembly and combinatorial products
tasks.goal: Expose strategy-specific inputs/junction checks and preserve all existing assembly products and limits.

tasks.title: CRISPR, codon optimization, BLAST and protein tools
tasks.goal: Preserve engines while adding explicit input/parameter review and accurate method/coverage labels.

tasks.title: Notebook creation, submission and local review
tasks.goal: Implement real blank/template drafts, stable submitted-result records and immutable local review revisions.

tasks.title: Typed Registry, relationships and deletion
tasks.goal: Federate typed entity references and implement record-specific archive/restore/dependency-aware deletion with tombstones.

tasks.title: Inventory assignment, transfer and snapshots
tasks.goal: Implement reviewed well/selection payloads, explicit units, collision checks and recoverable transfer plans.

tasks.title: Workflows and request handoffs
tasks.goal: Make task/request selection and graph execution status explicit and recoverable across module handoffs.

tasks.title: Insights scope, chart alternatives and export
tasks.goal: Bind dashboards to reviewed local data scope and preserve table/chart/CSV behavior with distinct empty/failure states.

tasks.title: Automation targets, journals and recovery
tasks.goal: Replace naive ingestion, dispatch explicit writeback targets and implement immutable pipeline revisions plus durable operation/recovery state.

tasks.title: Biologics, chemistry and RNA identities
tasks.goal: Apply the shared record/selection/result model to specialist inputs without replacing supported scientific methods.

tasks.title: In-vivo and bioprocess stateful records
tasks.goal: Preserve study/measurement/cohort and recipe/run/replicate behavior with explicit IDs, units and lifecycle controls.

tasks.title: Responsive, focus, error and accessibility hardening
tasks.goal: Complete runtime interaction states, semantic exposure, keyboard flow, panel behavior and measured dense-data rendering.

tasks.title: End-to-end validation and staged release
tasks.goal: Run the full regression/edge/UI checklist and first-user study, update traceability and ship only genuinely implemented behavior.
